root_cause: Segment._split_cells guesses a starting char index pos = int((cut / cell_length) * (len(text) - 1)) to skip ahead, then only walks FORWARD. With mixed single/double-width text (CJK + ASCII) the proportional guess can land past the cut, so cell_len(text[:pos]) > cut already; the forward loop never hits cell_pos == cut, immediately takes the 'cell_pos > cut' branch and returns a left segment wider than the cut (e.g. cut=7 on '早乙女リリエル (CV: 徳井青）' returned '早乙女リ ' = 9 cells).
best_solution: Make the starting guess never overshoot. Gold changes it to pos = int((cut / cell_length) * len(text)) - 1, clamped to 0, so text[:pos] starts at or before the cut cell and the existing forward walk (add cell_size(char) until cell_pos == cut, or split a straddled double-width char into two spaces) lands on the right position. Reasoning from the statement: the method's contract is cell_len(left) == cut and cell_len(right) == total - cut for every cut; a forward-only scan is only correct if its start is <= cut, so either bias the estimate down or start at 0 (O(n) but always correct). Also added a docstring noting the two-spaces behavior.
acceptable_alternatives: Start the scan at pos=0/cell_pos=0 (v6, v7) or rewrite the loop as a plain linear scan from 0 (v4); all correct, just lose the skip-ahead optimization. Walking backward when the guess overshoots would also work.
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_segment.py adds test_split_cells_mixed ('早乙女リリエル (CV: 徳井青）'), test_split_cells_doubles ('早'*20) and test_split_cells_single ('A'*20): for every position in range(1, cell_length), Segment.split_cells(seg, position) must give cell_len(left.text) == position and cell_len(right.text) == cell_length - position (imports rich.cells.cell_len). No new API.
locating_signals: Statement names the exact method `Segment._split_cells` (rich/segment.py) and says 'fix split cells'; the linked Textual issue only says a double-width character is measured incorrectly. The gold function is named; the defect (overshooting index heuristic) must be found by reading the 30-line function or by brute-forcing all cut positions on a mixed CJK string.
our_outcome_summary: v4, v6, v7 passed; v8 failed. v4 rewrote the loop as a linear scan from index 0 (correct). v6/v7 replaced the proportional guess with pos=0/cell_pos=0 (correct, slower). v8 made no behavioral change: it only inserted a comment after the double-width-split branch, so test_split_cells_mixed still failed with cell_len('早乙女リ ') == 9 != 7. v8 spent the most time (117 s, 26 calls) and ended with a no-op patch instead of verifying against a brute-force invariant check.
generalizable_lesson: When the statement is just 'fix <function>' with no repro, derive the function's invariant (here: left width == cut for every cut) and brute-force it over all inputs in a small loop, including mixed-width/unicode strings, before and after editing; any shortcut or estimate that feeds a one-directional loop must be checked for overshoot. Never submit a patch that only adds comments or docstrings: run the self-written invariant check and confirm it fails before the edit and passes after.
